The authors successfully reimplement key baselines (DDS, DensePure, DiffSmooth) using the same ViT backbone, allowing for a fair comparison of the algorithmic contribution rather than architectural superiority. The paper compares its ViT-based approach against a ResNet-based DDS baseline from the original paper, failing to isolate the algorithm from the architecture. It is highly likely that the observed improvements on CIFAR-10 are driven by the superior power of ViT rather than the rRCM training strategy, undermining the claim of generalization without further evidence.

Furthermore, the paper lacks necessary ablation studies to justify the complex two-stage pipeline (contrastive pre-training + consistency fine-tuning). Without isolating the contribution of the contrastive loss versus the consistency loss, or comparing against other self-supervised pre-training methods (like MoCo or DINO), it remains unclear if the proposed "consistency regularization" is actually the driving force or merely a component of standard strong ViT training practices.
